Repo /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa, branch feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui.

You are WAVE 2 of a two-wave review. Four agents have reported. Your job has two halves: **argue the opposite case, then reconcile.** Do not simply agree with them — I framed their questions, so their agreement may be an artefact of my framing rather than the evidence.

=== WHAT WAVE 1 CONCLUDED ===

**A — Scope ledger.** Diff is +4,739/−105 over 47 files (+ 2 untracked = 4,888 lines / 49 files). Categorised: REQUIRED 38% · SUPPORTING 23% · DEFERRED 13% · UNMENTIONED 25%. So 38% is deferred-by-the-story or never-mentioned. Modal = 633 lines / 13%, none of it executing in production. `button.ts` went from 2 variants × 2 sizes to 6 × 3; `primaryInverse`/`secondaryInverse` have zero consumers. `clearable` has zero consumers. `contentfulSchema.placeholder.ts` has zero importers. AC7 has zero coverage anywhere.

**B — Cost of carry.** Modal bundle is only 3,989 B min / ~1.6 kB gzip = 0.88% of the 180 kB budget, so bundle weight is NOT the problem. But `useSubscribeModal.test.tsx` is 204 ms of 424 ms total suite time (48%) for dead UI. `recipeGuards.test.ts` costs 1.22 ms — effectively free. **ZimmButton and ZimmTextInput have ZERO direct live render sites** — every direct call site is inside the never-rendering modal; the live footer renders one button and one text input, both via ZimmInputAction. `footer.ts` has 30 Figma refs across 11 node IDs, all 30 in the non-modal region, zero in the 9 modal parts. Review burden ≈ 10–12 hours vs the playbook's 1-hour budget; ~31 Tier 1 lines gate the whole 49-file PR. It contradicted A on the chevrons: all four MUST exist because base SFCC imports them across pagination, locale-selector, accordion, product-scroller, promo-code, account, PLP and page-designer.

**C — Opportunity cost.** AC2, AC3 met. AC5 met as placeholder but its a11y note is NOT. AC1 not met on /checkout (Salesforce demo footer, "Orders made WILL NOT be processed"). AC4 not met at ≥384px (wraps to 2 columns; every current phone width lands there). AC6 partial. AC7 not met and the drafted schema is per-LOCALE where AC7 needs per-STOREFRONT (UK and EU-domestic both serve en-GB, needing different currency and legal links). Zero react-intl for ~14 chrome strings on fr/it/es storefronts, and i18n extraction is silently broken for every `.tsx` override. The 24px WCAG floor was implemented on the opt-in `clearButton` nobody renders, not on the submit button the story's note names.

**D — Audit the audit.** 53% of the 55 commits were behaviour/defect fixes. But the final 13-item pass was 1 of 13 perceptible (and only under browser zoom) — marginal value fell ~6× at one identifiable commit, `9ec0740` (16:51). The three original theme guards were each written after a shipped defect (3 for 3); the three added this session protect zero live instances (0 for 3). Common cause of the session's bad checks: *the verification instrument was built from the same belief as the thing it verified, and was never made to fail on purpose.* Its headline: every item on the missed list lives OUTSIDE the working tree — GitHub review threads, a font licence, a memory doc, a site-config table.

=== ESTABLISHED FACTS, VERIFIED BY ME — do not re-litigate these ===
- **safeHref has a LIVE bypass.** `isSafeHref('/\\example.com')` → true, resolving to `https://example.com/`. Same for `/\\/evil.com`. The 13 committed test cases contain zero backslashes. Confirmed by execution.
- **The subscribe submit button is 16×16** — measured three times in Chromium, padding 0px. Chakra's IconButton hard-sets `padding:"0"` as a style prop, beating `button.ts`'s `sizes.icon = {p:'xs'}`, which is therefore dead code. D's claim that it computes to 32×32 was a derivation and is WRONG.
- `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` is clean; Hard Rule #3 is not breached.
- The font `.woff2` are committed, `ZimmFontFace` mounts unconditionally in the production `_app-config` shell, and `staticFolderCopyPlugin` copies `app/static` in both client and SSR builds — so they publish to the MRT CDN. The Tier 1 rule text claiming "development and testing" is not implemented anywhere.

=== YOUR HALF ONE: STEELMAN THE WORK ===
Argue, with evidence from the repo, the strongest possible case that this branch is NOT overengineered. Specifically attack these Wave 1 conclusions:

1. **The atoms.** B says ZimmButton/ZimmTextInput have zero direct live render sites. Counter-argument to test: `.claude/rules/components.md` and the FED playbook mandate "all variants designed upfront" precisely BECAUSE the Contentful sync is additive-only and getting a variant model wrong is semi-permanent. Is building the full variant surface now actually the *cheaper* path? Check whether other in-flight or upcoming stories consume these atoms (grep the repo, check `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md`, look for other branches via `git branch -a`).
2. **The 38-part recipe.** `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` mandates a theme recipe as the single canonical styling surface and forbids inline styles and `.zimm-*` class mirrors. Given that constraint, how much of those 546 lines was actually optional? Would a smaller footer have needed materially fewer parts?
3. **The guards.** D says 0 for 3 on the new ones. But Group A's S3 reportedly found a live 3-element responsive array in the shipped theme (`header.ts:56,59`) that every prop-keyed guard was structurally blind to. And S1 (the non-empty precondition) is the change that makes the OTHER four guards mean anything. Is "0 live instances" the right metric for a guard, or is that like judging a smoke detector by fires?
4. **The modal.** It is 633 lines that never execute. But HPC-035/037 are CONFIRMED requirements in `.docs/prd/homepage.md` §6. Does HPC-035 inherit something genuinely valuable — a working focus trap, scroll lock, tested state machine — or something that gets rewritten? Read the code and judge.
5. **The audit loop.** D says it went negative after 16:51. But the loop is what FOUND the descope, the 22px layout shift, and (indirectly) the safeHref bypass. Is there a version of this where the "wasted" passes were the cost of discovering the valuable findings, and couldn't have been targeted in advance?

=== YOUR HALF TWO: RECONCILE ===
Then resolve the disagreements and produce the actual answer. Required outputs:

**(a) Resolve A vs B on the chevrons** — A said unused, B said mandatory. Determine which is right by checking base SFCC imports yourself.
**(b) Resolve A vs D on safeHref** — A called it SUPPORTING-but-weak ("nothing breaks without it today"); D found a live bypass inside it. Are both true simultaneously? What does that imply about the value of the util vs the value of its tests?
**(c) The honest scope percentage.** A says 38% deferred-or-unmentioned. After your steelman, what is the defensible number? Show your adjustment.
**(d) Three lists, with the AC as arbiter, not code quality:**
   - **KEEP** — stays in this PR, with the justification
   - **STRIP** — should come out of this PR (to a follow-up branch, or deleted), with the cost of removing it now vs later
   - **FIX** — must be fixed before merge, ranked by shopper/rollout risk
   For STRIP, be concrete about mechanics: what can actually be lifted cleanly, and what is too entangled to be worth unpicking now.
**(e) The single highest-value next action**, and why it beats the alternatives.

=== ACCURACY REQUIREMENTS ===
- Your steelman must be genuine, not a rhetorical exercise. If an item cannot be defended, say so plainly.
- Where you overturn a Wave 1 conclusion, show the evidence.
- Do not use "it's good practice" as a justification for anything. Tie every KEEP to an AC, a mandated rule you can cite by file, or a measured cost saving.
- The user is the FED Lead who ran this loop and asked for this review. Neither flattery nor performative harshness is useful. Give them the number and the three lists.
- Read-only. Modify nothing. Do not run `npm start`. You may use the dev server on :3000 and `npx vitest run` / `npx tsc --noEmit`; do NOT build Storybook.

# WAVE 2: STEELMAN, THEN RECONCILE

Read-only throughout. `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0; `npx vitest run` is 190/190 green in 2.19s.

First, a scope correction that affects everything below: **the PR is not 47 files.** The working tree carries +292/−96 uncommitted across 10 files plus 149 untracked lines (`useSubscribeModal.test.tsx` 123, `theme/components/zimmLogo.ts` 26 — the latter *is* registered and consumed). Real total ≈ **4,982 added lines / 49 files**.

---

## HALF ONE — STEELMAN

### 1. The atoms — STEELMAN FAILS, but B's framing is wrong too

**The mandate does not exist.** No "all variants designed upfront" text exists anywhere on this branch or on `develop` — not in `.claude/rules/components.md`, not in `AGENTS.md`, not in `.docs/`. There is no `f2r/` directory on this branch at all. The nearest mandates live on *other* branches (`f2r-implementation-workflow`, `f2r-component-registry`) and govern a **kebab-case, explicitly Chakra-free** pipeline (`convert-to-uikit/SKILL.md:34`) that these camelCase Chakra-based atoms are not the output of. The Contentful-additive-only argument also doesn't transfer: these are React prop unions, not Contentful content-type fields. Nothing about them is semi-permanent.

Worse for the steelman: **three parallel ui-kit tracks now exist, none consuming another**, and `overrides/app/components/button/index.tsx` (pre-existing, 9 July) is a Zimmermann button wrapper with **zero** consumers sitting next to the new `ZimmButton`. Nothing in the repo would have flagged that — `.claude/rules/components.md` has no "check the registry before creating" rule and `AGENTS.md` contains zero occurrences of "registry". The most obvious future consumer, SFCC-89/91 PDP, built `zimmPageToolbar` instead of using `ZimmButton`; the header was already built without `ZimmNavItem`/`ZimmLogo`/`ZimmButton`.

**But I overturn B's headline.** "ZimmButton and ZimmTextInput have ZERO direct live render sites" is true only of the word *direct*. Both render in production: `zimmInputAction/index.tsx:61` renders `ZimmTextInput`, `:70` renders `ZimmButton`, and `ZimmInputAction` is rendered by the live footer at `footer/index.tsx:238`. All six atoms have a production path. What is speculative is the **unreached surface inside them**: 33 of 37 `ZimmIcon` types, `clearable`, `size='large'` (the *default*), `fullWidth`, `helperText`, controlled `value`. The atoms are justified; their interiors are over-built.

Also worth knowing: `zimmTextInput/index.tsx:38` cites `f2r/02-design/specs/components/text-input.md`, **which does not exist on this branch**.

### 2. The 38-part recipe — STEELMAN SUCCEEDS

I checked every part against its consumer. **Zero dead parts — all 38 are referenced in `footer/index.tsx`.** 29 serve the live footer; 9 are `modal*`. `overrideStyling.md` §hierarchy item 3 plus "One canonical styling surface per component type" genuinely forecloses the alternatives (inline `sx`, `.zimm-*` mirrors), and the part count is set by the number of distinct styled elements in the Figma design (3 nav columns + subscribe + logo + bottom bar carrying copyright, legal links and locale). A smaller footer would need fewer parts only by having fewer elements. **~29 parts is close to the structural floor under the rule this repo mandates.** The only reducible portion is the 9 modal parts (`footer.ts:197–247`, ~51 lines).

### 3. The guards — STEELMAN SUCCEEDS for S1, and "0 live instances" is the wrong metric

S1 is not a fifth guard, it is the **precondition that makes the other four non-vacuous**. Every other test asserts `expect(offenders).toEqual([])`, which an empty input satisfies exactly as well as a clean one — the test's own comment says deleting `components` would turn the whole file green. That is precisely D's diagnosed root cause ("the instrument was never made to fail on purpose"), so scoring S1 as 0-for-3 on live instances applies the wrong yardstick to the one item that fixed the yardstick.

"0 live instances" is generally the wrong metric: a regression guard's value is (recurrence probability × recurrence cost), and the whole file costs **2ms** (`recipeGuards.test.ts`, 5 tests). Smoke-detector logic holds.

**Where the steelman must concede:** the guards' own docblock admits they cannot see JSX props — and that blind spot is *currently occupied*. `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:302` has `fontSize="l"`, which emits nothing. I verified it is **pre-existing on `develop`** (line 293 there), so it is not this PR's regression, but it means the exact bug class these guards were built for is live in a place they structurally cannot reach.

### 4. The modal — STEELMAN FAILS on mechanics, SUCCEEDS on copy and state machine

HPC-035 and HPC-037 are genuinely confirmed (`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.docs/prd/homepage.md:89,91`). So the question is only whether HPC-035 *inherits* or *rewrites*. I read the code: it rewrites.

Chakra is at **2.7.0** and exports `Modal`/`ModalOverlay`/`ModalContent`/`ModalHeader`/`ModalBody`/`ModalFooter`/`ModalCloseButton`/`useDisclosure` — all verified importable. `react-focus-lock` and `react-remove-scroll` are already installed. Base SFCC uses Chakra `<Modal>` in **28 files**, including `use-auth-modal` — which this repo lists as a Tier 2 *shared hook*. So `useSubscribeModal.ts` reimplements installed, battle-tested infrastructure, and does it less correctly:

- No `inert`/`aria-hidden` on background content — screen-reader users can still traverse the page behind the dialog.
- The Tab trap only fires when `document.activeElement` is already `first` or `last`; focus arriving from anywhere else is not corralled, and everything behind the modal remains tabbable.
- `document.body.style.overflow = 'hidden'` with no scrollbar-width compensation (layout shift) and no iOS Safari handling — `react-remove-scroll`, already in `node_modules`, does both.

That contradicts `AGENTS.md` > Performance > Dependencies ("check `package.json` for what is already installed") and DRY in `conventions.md`. **What genuinely survives HPC-035:** the two HPC-037 copy constants, the two-step `PendingSignup` state machine with its explicit "never show false success" discipline, and the 9 theme parts — roughly 60 of ~371 lines.

**I also overturn Wave 1's size figure.** Measured modal footprint: 91 lines of `footer/index.tsx` (71–161) + 51 lines of `footer.ts` (197–247) + 106 (`useSubscribeModal.ts`) + 123 (untracked test) = **~371 lines, not 633.**

### 5. The audit loop — STEELMAN PARTIALLY SUCCEEDS, but not on the example given

The general claim is sound: re-reading found the descope and the 22px layout shift, and you cannot target a re-read in advance — that is the irreducible cost of the method.

**But the safeHref example is backwards. The loop did not find that bypass; the loop shipped it.** `safeHref.ts`'s own docblock says "a protocol-relative `//host` silently leaves the site… it was a real bypass, closed in e9c2180" — while leaving `/\` and `/\t` wide open and committing 13 test cases containing zero backslashes. That is D's diagnosed failure mode executing verbatim: the test was written from the same belief as the fix. So the honest read is that the loop had positive marginal value while it was reading *code* and negative value once it began reading *its own conclusions*. D's 16:51 inflection is a fair marker for that transition.

---

## HALF TWO — RECONCILE

### (a) Chevrons: **B is right; A is wrong** — and it is more load-bearing than B said

It was a **move, not an addition** (commit `c3f6982`). `overrides/app/components/icons/index.tsx` is a *selective* re-export — line 8 is `export * from './zimm'`, and the enumerated base list **terminates** at line 73 with no `export *`. The branch deleted the four chevrons from that base list (lines 19–22, now a comment) and re-supplied them from `zimm.tsx:102,108,114,120`. Because the PWA Kit override resolver (`overrides-plugin.js:101-103,135-145`) redirects every base-template import of that path into this barrel, `zimm.tsx` is now the **sole source** of those four names for **22 base-SFCC import sites** — pagination, breadcrumb, promo-code, nested-accordion, locale-selector, product-scroller, page-designer carousel, basic-tile, ask-assistant-banner, list-menu-trigger, account, PLP. Deleting them as "dead code" gives you a passing build and a runtime `Element type is invalid… got: undefined`, and TypeScript cannot see the base `.jsx` consumers at all.

Latent trap of the same pattern, pre-existing and currently unreachable: the enumerated list omits `FigmaLogo`/`GithubLogo`, which base `pages/home/data.js:16` imports.

### (b) safeHref: **both are true simultaneously**

A is right on reachability. Every href the util guards arrives from `FOOTER_FIXTURE`, a developer-authored constant (`footer/index.tsx:549`). No attacker-controlled value reaches `isSafeHref` today. D is right on the code. Reconciliation: **the util is a pre-positioned guard whose data source is not connected yet.** It goes hot at `footer/index.tsx:536`, when HPC-034 swaps in the Contentful CDA fetch.

The bypass is **wider than reported.** Executed:

```
ALLOW  "/\\example.com"   -> https://example.com/
ALLOW  "/\\/evil.com"     -> https://evil.com/
ALLOW  "/\t/evil.com"     -> https://evil.com/     <- not previously reported
block  "//evil.com"       -> https://evil.com/
```

A TAB also passes, because the WHATWG URL parser strips C0/whitespace *before* parsing. So the fix is **not** "add `\\` to the lookahead" — it is "reject backslash **and** strip-or-reject C0 control + whitespace before testing."

Implication for value: **keep the util, distrust its tests.** `safeHref.test.ts` costs 1ms — the cheapest artefact in the PR — and is the only one that actively misled, because it encodes the author's model of the threat rather than the threat.

### (c) The honest scope percentage: **17–25%, not 38%**

| Adjustment | Lines | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| A's figure | — | 38% deferred-or-unmentioned |
| `icons/zimm.tsx` reclassified REQUIRED (22 base import sites) | −185 | mandatory, not unused |
| Modal remeasured (371, not 633) | −262 | arithmetic |
| All 38 recipe parts consumed → no dead recipe weight | −0 | removes an assumed deduction |
| `icon`/`iconInverse` variants consumed by `zimmInputAction:71` | −~40 | only 2 of 4 new variants are dead |
| **7 stories mandated** by `components.md` > Storybook ("Required for any component exported from its folder") | **−1,181** | largest single correction |

Remaining deferred-or-unmentioned, measured: modal 371 · `contentfulSchema.placeholder.ts` 97 (zero importers) · `primaryInverse`+`secondaryInverse` ~78 (zero consumers anywhere, including the modal) · `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` 189 · AI-config/registry doc churn 104 · `.storybook` 14 · theme/font tests 415.

- **Strict (tests counted as unmentioned): 1,268 / 4,982 = 25%**
- **Tests kept under `AGENTS.md` > Testing (they cost 2ms + 1ms + 3ms + 51ms): 853 / 4,982 = 17%**

**Defensible number: 17–25%.** The 38% figure was inflated mostly by counting mandated stories and mandatory icons as discretionary.

### (d) Three lists — AC as arbiter

**KEEP**

| Item | Justification (AC / citable rule / measured cost) |
|---|---|
| `footer/index.tsx` non-modal (~450) + `footer.ts` 29 non-modal parts | AC1–AC6; `overrideStyling.md` §hierarchy item 3 |
| `icons/zimm.tsx` (185) | Mandatory — sole source for 22 base-SFCC import sites |
| All 6 atoms + all 7 stories (1,181) | Every atom has a production path via `zimmInputAction`; stories **required** by `components.md` > Storybook |
| `zimmNavItem.ts` / `zimmTextInput.ts` / `zimmLogo.ts` | `overrideStyling.md` "One canonical styling surface per component type" |
| `contentfulFixture.ts` (134) | Live production data source, `footer/index.tsx:549` |
| `types/contentful.ts` (55) | `AGENTS.md` > Type Definitions |
| `safeHref.ts` (15) | Goes hot at HPC-034; keep the util, fix it (see FIX #2) |
| `recipeGuards.test.ts` (241) | 2ms measured; S1 makes the other four assertions non-vacuous |
| `button.ts` `icon` + `iconInverse` | Consumed at `zimmInputAction/index.tsx:71` |

Note: `button.ts`'s diff is **purely additive** (123 insertions, 0 deletions; `defaultProps` pre-existed on `develop`). "2×2 → 6×3" is correct arithmetic but zero blast radius — an unnamed variant key cannot change any existing render.

**STRIP**

*Clean lifts, near-zero mechanics:*
1. `contentfulSchema.placeholder.ts` (97) — zero importers. Cost now ~0; cost later it rots against the real content type.
2. `primaryInverse` + `secondaryInverse` (~78) — zero consumers anywhere. Additive keys; removal cannot change a render. Cost now ~0.
3. `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` (189) + the 4 AI-config docs (104) — no AC, independent files, ~15 min. **This also removes `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` from the diff, which is Tier 1 Governance** — its presence is why this PR currently spans Tier 1 + Tier 2 + untiered in one change, against Hard Rule #10.

*Separable with moderate effort:*
4. The modal (371 across 4 files). `enableNameCapture` is already a single boolean gate, so the lift is mechanical: move `useSubscribeModal.ts` + its untracked test + the `SubscribeModal` component + the 9 `modal*` parts to the HPC-035 branch; **keep** the two HPC-037 copy constants and the `PendingSignup`/`SubmitState` machine, which `handleEmailSubmit`'s descope path uses. ~1 hour.
   **Strip it on mechanics, not on weight.** If HPC-035 is next sprint, strip-then-rebuild churn roughly cancels the carry cost — so lines are not the argument. The argument is that hand-rolled focus-trap/scroll-lock is the wrong pattern in a repo where base SFCC uses Chakra `<Modal>` 28 times, and shipping it creates a precedent the next modal copies.

*Too entangled to be worth unpicking now:*
- The 33 unused `ZimmIcon` types — union and map are one structure, and the glyphs are needed by base SFCC regardless. Leave; note as unexercised in the PR body.
- `clearable` (~15 lines woven through the recipe's `filled`/`focused` prop logic). Leave; note it.
- Fonts — the blocker is the licence, not the code (see FIX #1).

**FIX** — ranked by shopper/rollout risk

1. **Unlicensed web font publishing to the public CDN.** `footer.ts:287` says in-repo: "Futura Round (**unlicensed for web**". The `.woff2` are committed, `ZimmFontFace` mounts unconditionally in the production `_app-config` shell, and `staticFolderCopyPlugin` copies `app/static` in both client and SSR builds. Meanwhile Tier 1 `frozenFiles.md` states the fonts are "self-hosted **for development and testing**" — **that gate is not implemented anywhere.** Legal exposure for a luxury brand, and currently invisible to anyone reading the rules.
2. **`/checkout` renders the Salesforce demo footer.** `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/_app/index.jsx:484` — `{!isCheckout ? <Footer /> : <CheckoutFooter />}`; `pages/checkout/partials/checkout-footer.jsx:70` contains *"This is a demo store only. Orders made WILL NOT be processed."* No override exists. Defeats AC1 on the highest-intent page, and the string actively tells shoppers their order won't process. (`isCheckout` is `/\/checkout$/` — verify sub-routes separately.)
3. **safeHref bypass** — regex plus tests, per (b). Latent today; blocks HPC-034.
4. **Subscribe submit button is 16×16** — WCAG 2.2 AA 2.5.8 (24×24). `sizes.icon`'s `p:'xs'` is dead because Chakra `IconButton` hard-sets `padding:"0"` as a style prop. Fix via `minW`/`minH` on the variant or in `ZimmButton`'s icon branch — not `p`. This is the control the story's own a11y note names.
5. **~14 hardcoded English strings, zero `react-intl`** in footer + atoms (verified: 0 matches for `react-intl|formatMessage|useIntl` across `footer/` and `ui-kits/`). Renders English on fr/it/es. **Correction to C: extraction is not broken** — `extract-default-messages.js:64` globs `"overrides/app/**/*.{js,jsx,ts,tsx}"`. The real wart is that the `.jsx`→`.tsx` rename defeats the `--ignore` de-dup at lines 57–59, so shadowed base messages stay in the catalogue. Separate and minor.
6. **Nav columns collapse to 1 column at ≤375px.** Measured in Chromium: 320/360/375 → 1 column; 384–~560 → 2; ≥~564 → 3; ≥768 → tablet rule. Threshold is exactly **384px = 140 + 40 + 140 + 64**. `footer.ts` itself says Figma specifies 2-col mobile. **This inverts C's finding:** phones at ≥384px (390, 393, 414, 430 — most current devices) get the *designed* 2-column layout; the defect is iPhone SE / 13-mini class at 375px getting an unintended single column. Real, but narrower and lower-severity than "every current phone width."
7. **AC7 per-storefront vs per-locale** — C's finding stands, and settle it *before* HPC-034 writes the content type; the Contentful sync is additive-only, so a wrong field shape is expensive to undo.
8. *Flag only, not this PR's regression:* `header/index.tsx:302` `fontSize="l"` emits nothing (pre-existing on `develop` at line 293).

Also drop from the cost ledger: **test time is not a cost.** Measured per-file — `useSubscribeModal.test.tsx` 184ms, `recipeGuards` 2ms, `safeHref` 1ms, `zimmTextInput` 3ms — against a **2.19s** whole-suite wall clock, running in parallel, where a single pre-existing `theme/index.test.tsx` case costs 205ms on its own. B's "48% of suite time" is arithmetically right and practically meaningless.

### (e) Single highest-value next action

**Resolve the Futura Round web licence — buy it, or gate the `@font-face` mount to non-production so the code matches what Tier 1 `frozenFiles.md` already claims.**

Why it beats the alternatives: it is the only item with legal and financial exposure outside the codebase; it is the only item where **the repo's own governing documentation actively misstates what the code does**, which means nobody reading the rules will ever look for it; and it is the only item whose resolution needs a human outside the squad (procurement/brand), so it has the longest lead time — raising it costs one message now and a launch later.

It beats the checkout footer (#2) precisely *because* the checkout footer will be caught. A demo-store string on the payment page is glaring and QA will find it in the first pass. An unlicensed font on the CDN will not be found, because the Tier 1 doc says it isn't happening. It beats the safeHref fix (latent until HPC-034 connects Contentful, so it can ride with that story), the 16×16 button (real WCAG failure, but one control and a two-line theme fix that can travel with the checkout-footer commit), and stripping the modal (hygiene, not risk — nothing breaks if it ships).

This is also the same class as D's own headline finding: **every item on the missed list lives outside the working tree.** This one is the largest of them, and it is still outside.

One mechanical note for #2 when you get to it: prefer overriding `pages/checkout/partials/checkout-footer` over touching the `isCheckout` branch in `_app/` — `_app/` is Tier 2 Global Shell requiring both squads, whereas `pages/checkout/partials/` is on neither protected list. It needs a copy-first step per `AGENTS.md`.
